name: Analytical ultracentrifugation
summary: Spinning solutions at very high speed while watching particles settle let scientists measure the size of proteins and other large molecules.
description: High-speed centrifugation with optical observation of sedimentation in solution to study sizes and molecular properties of dispersed material.

Svedberg contrasts earlier gravity sedimentation and lower-speed centrifugation with high-field optical sedimentation measurements.

events.statement: By November 1924, Svedberg and visiting researcher Fåhraeus had used ultracentrifugation in haemoglobin research.
events.caveats: The visiting scientist worked with the developer, so this is collaborative research use rather than an independent laboratory installation. The original 1926 paper was inaccessible; later scholarly accounts support the use. Adair independently measured the weight by another method.

evidence.supports: The scholarly discussion describes Svedberg and Fåhraeus’s 1926 haemoglobin research using equilibrium ultracentrifugation and notes Adair’s independent earlier estimate.
